fulltext: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据韩国媒体 ZDNet 昨日（10 月 15 日）报道，为了降低对单一供应商的依赖，三星正考虑为 Galaxy 手机的 OLED 显示驱动芯片（DDI）引入第二家代工合作伙伴，美国晶圆代工厂格芯（GlobalFoundries）成为主要评估对象。
IT之家注：显示驱动芯片（Display Driver IC，简称 DDI）把处理器送来的图像数据，转换成屏幕每个像素能理解的电压、电流和时序信号，从而决定画面亮什么、暗什么、显示什么颜色，因此可视为手机屏幕的“交通指挥系统”。
在 OLED 手机中，DDI 尤其关键。OLED 像素自发光，DDI 需要精确控制每个像素的电流和灰度，以实现高对比度、广色域、高刷新率，同时尽量降低功耗。三星的移动 DDI 还支持可变刷新率，例如在 1Hz 至 144Hz 之间动态调整，以在流畅滚动、游戏和静态画面之间平衡体验与续航。
报道指出，由于 Galaxy Z Fold8 市场需求超出预期，三星此前联系联华电子（UMC，下文简称联电）要求追加生产 DDI，但联电的 22 纳米 DDI 产线已满负荷运转，无法承接紧急订单。这直接导致三星不得不削减 Z Fold8 部分零部件的 9 月生产计划，并顺延至 10 月，拖累了出货节奏与营收表现。
为此三星考虑打破 Galaxy OLED 手机 DDI 由联电独家代工的格局，避免再度出现类似生产瓶颈，消息称三星正在考察格芯位于新加坡和德国的 22 纳米、28 纳米生产设施。
若合作落地，格芯代工的 DDI 芯片最快可能在 2027 年底进入 Galaxy 手机供应链，并率先用于搭载 OLED 屏幕的中低端 Galaxy A 系列机型。三星目前尚未正式公布相关供应安排，格芯能否获得订单仍取决于产能、良率、成本及认证测试等因素。

cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】Scaling Indic Pretraining: 2.8 Trillion Tokens and an Open Data Generation Pipeline
fulltext: What is in the corpus? From English source documents to Indic training data The twelve-language workflow The ten-language workflow What changed after Indic continued pretraining? Broader Indic capabilities in Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Start building Load the corpus Adapt the generation recipe Scope and limitations Further reading and acknowledgments Native-script data for 22 languages, romanized data for twelve, and a reusable GPU-accelerated pipeline for translation, quality assessment, and repair.

Authors: AI4Bharat — Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan, Mitesh Khapra, Anoop Kunchukuttan. NVIDIA — Niket Agarwal, Raviraj Joshi, Anusha Kamath, Markus Kliegl, Yev Meyer, Sriharsha Niverty, Kiran Praveen, Utkarsh Vaidya.

We're excited to introduce Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1 approximately 2.8 trillion tokens across 22 Indian languages, releasing soon alongside the open, GPU-accelerated data generation pipeline used to create it. These are the 22 languages listed in India's Constitution: the first languages for 97% of Indians, or nearly 1.2 billion citizens at the 2011 Census. Developed by NVIDIA with IIT Madras, India's premier engineering institute, and its AI4Bharat lab, this release gives model builders a substantial new resource for Indic pretraining. The pipeline captures the full generation recipe, including prompts, LLM workflows, and quality checks, so developers can adapt it to their own source material and generate more data for their needs.

AI4Bharat, IIT Madras' Indian language research lab, builds open-source datasets and models for Indian languages. Its resources, such as Sangraha, an open pretraining corpus for 22 Indian languages, have helped lay the foundation for open Indic language-model research. Our joint open-source release represents a substantial expansion of the open synthetic Indic training data that will be available to the community. It brings a broad mix of curated English material, including mathematics, code, and question-answer content, into Indian languages, giving teams more training material for building models that can explain technical concepts, work through problems, and answer questions in those languages. Every record traces back to a curated source document, and each output is checked against its input, so the synthetic text stays grounded in real information.

Mitesh Khapra, who heads AI4Bharat and made the 2025 TIME100 AI list, has named the core problem: Indian language technology trails English because "we do not have enough data for Indian languages." We're answering that call with more data, plus an open recipe for generating more.

The corpus also accounts for how people write. It includes native-script data for all 22 languages and romanized text for twelve, spanning 34 language-script configurations. Our workflows combine document-level translation, quality assessment, and targeted repair, with checks to preserve content such as equations, tables, and code. This data complements naturally authored Indic text, which remains essential for local knowledge and cultural context.

We're sharing the open generation recipe so the community can not just reproduce the data but take this work further. Teams can use the corpus directly, adapt the prompts and quality checks, or bring their own source documents to the workflow. By opening up both the data and the process, we aim to make large-scale Indic data generation more accessible and enable more developers to contribute to stronger models across Indian languages.

Continued pretraining for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL added 10 billion Indic tokens, drawn from a twelve-language subset of this corpus and natural Indic text. Our technical report on the model covers the full story. We plan to build on this corpus in future Nemotron models.

Figure 1. The corpus contains 2,601.0 billion native-script tokens and 224.6 billion romanized tokens. Counts use the Gemma-4 tokenizer. Document records include translations and script variants of shared sources; they are not counts of unique English documents.
The corpus has two groups of language configurations:

Here, native-script describes the writing system: the text is still translated from English. Romanized means Indic-language text written in Latin script, not an English translation. For each of the twelve dual-script languages, romanization covers a subset of the accepted native-script translations.

This distinction matters when constructing a training mixture. Native and romanized records offer different script exposure, but can express the same underlying content. The token counts describe the retained corpus, including accepted rewrites, rather than a training run's token budget. Counts also depend on the tokenizer used, so corpus inventory and training-token counts should be read separately.

To build this corpus, we start with documents from 15 Nemotron-CC-v2 subsets, covering web text, question-answer material, mathematics, code, and other specialized content. We use NeMo Data Designer, NVIDIA's open-source framework for generating synthetic data, to run translation, quality checks, and targeted repair. Throughout the workflow, we retain each source identifier so developers can trace an output back to its original document. Clear provenance like this is part of what makes open data practical to audit and build on. Figure 2 shows the workflow for twelve languages.

Figure 2. Four-stage Indic synthetic-data pipeline for twelve languages, implemented using NeMo Data Designer and Gemma-4-31B-it. We translate English documents, assess translation quality, repair low-scoring outputs, and convert a subset of accepted translations into Latin script. The other ten languages use the separate Indic Translate workflow described below.

For these twelve languages, we translate documents in full so the model can use context across paragraphs, tables, and equations. We selected Gemma-4-31B-it by comparing models on complete documents, checking translation quality and preservation of technical content. Our prompts distinguish prose to translate from content to preserve, including code, equations, URLs, and formatting.

After translation, we use the same model to assess each output against its English source. A rubric inspired by Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM), an open framework for classifying translation errors by type and severity, covers meaning, fluency, terminology, style, and formatting. We retain only outputs scoring at least 75 out of 100 (a rubric score, not an accuracy percentage). For lower-scoring outputs, we use the assessment feedback to guide repairs, then reassess them against the same threshold. This process recovered 438.4 billion tokens across native-script and romanized data, already included in the corpus total. Sampled human reviews and tests with deliberately introduced errors helped identify omissions and residual English, informing improvements to our prompts and checks.

Accepted native-script translations also provide the starting point for romanized data. We convert a subset into Latin script and check each result against its native-script input. This separates translation from script conversion. In our initial human comparison, this two-step approach produced fewer hallucinated additions and less residual English than generating romanized text directly from English.

For the other ten languages, we adapt the workflow to address long-document quality and script-stability issues observed in our comparisons. We translate with Indic Translate, a document-level translation model for English and 22 Indian languages from Bodhan AI, a nonprofit center for AI in education incubated at IIT Madras. Gemma-4-31B-it then assesses each translation against its English source. For eight languages, we keep the whole-document approach. For longer Santali documents, we translate overlapping windows and reconstruct the document; for Manipuri, we translate into Bengali script before converting to Meitei Mayek, its native script. These workflows retain outputs scoring at least 75 out of 100 and produce native-script data only, without feedback-based rewriting.

The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL technical report compares the checkpoint immediately before Indic continued pretraining (CPT) with the checkpoint after that stage. The configured budget was 100 billion training tokens, with 10% (10 billion tokens) allocated to a mixture of synthetic and natural Indic text. The remaining 90% maintained the preceding training mixture's relative proportions.
Scores increased on all five reported Indic knowledge and reasoning benchmarks: MILU, Indic MMLU-Pro, Indic ARC-Challenge, Indic ARC-Easy, and Indic GSM8K.

Figure 3. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL before and after the Indic CPT stage. Gains range from 4.98 to 9.82 percentage points. The comparison reports the change across a training stage that combines synthetic and natural Indic data, rather than isolating the synthetic corpus's contribution. Language coverage differs by benchmark; these are stage-level checkpoints, not a comparison of final model releases.
Source: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL technical report, Table 2. GSM8K excludes Odia because evaluation exceeded the serving context limit.
These gains support the combined synthetic-and-natural Indic CPT recipe, while leaving the choice of mixture for other models and languages to further study.

The companion Indic report examines source mixtures, synthetic-data pool size, and script coverage using first-pass accepted data for the twelve-language group. Evaluating the full corpus, including recovered rewrites and the other ten languages, remains a next step for those controlled studies.

Beyond the CPT-stage results, how does the released model compare with the previous generation? Figure 4 compares Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with Nemotron 3 Super across Indic task performance and language quality. These results reflect the released model's full training pipeline, including Indic CPT and post-training.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL scores higher on five of the six task benchmarks shown, spanning knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, code, and translation. Instruction following on IFEval 1.5 dipped 2.04 points. It also improves across all four IndiVibe dimensions: usefulness, fluency, language and script fidelity, and appropriate verbosity. IndiVibe is Sarvam AI's open benchmark of assistant-style prompts in Indian languages. Together, these evaluations examine both what the model can do and how well it communicates in Indian languages.

Figure 4. Indic task performance and language quality across Nemotron Super generations. Left: six task benchmarks. Right: preliminary IndiVibe conditional preference scores, not direct head-to-head win rates. Labels show changes in percentage points, except WMT24++, which uses chrF points. See the companion Indic technical report for benchmark and evaluation details.

Start with the languages and scripts your model needs, inspect a sample, and review the dataset card and license before training. Configurations use language, script, and region tags: for example, hi-Deva-IN denotes Hindi in Devanagari, while hi-Latn-IN denotes romanized Hindi.
The example below asks for the repository ID from the dataset card, then discovers the available splits and streams a sample.
Hugging Face Datasets supports streaming so readers can inspect records without downloading the entire corpus. Once the release is available, pin a dataset revision for reproducible experiments.

For a first training study, compare mixtures at a fixed token budget and record the natural/synthetic and native/romanized shares. Track per-language results alongside English capability retention and language/script quality. When creating held-out splits, account for records derived from the same source across languages and scripts.

To build a fuller recipe, pair the corpus with Nemotron post-training data, such as the Chat & Instruction or Post-Training Blends collections. For India-specific synthetic data, seed NeMo Data Designer with Nemotron-Personas-India, synthetic personas in English and Hindi grounded in real-world distributions for India.

The open-source Nemotron Bharat translation plugin for NeMo Data Designer provides translation and evaluation prompts, optional feedback-based rewriting, document windowing, and script-remapping support. Use its configuration reference to choose models and languages, adapt prompts to your domain, and set rewrite parameters. The accompanying developer note explains the workflow and engineering choices.

Start with a small sample of your own source documents. Inspect translation quality and preservation of code, mathematics, and formatting, then refine the prompts and checks with native-language reviewers before scaling up. Treat generation and corpus acceptance as separate steps: the plugin returns candidates and scores, while your filtering policy determines which records enter the training corpus.

Translation broadens access to the source material, but does not replace text originally written in Indian languages or guarantee coverage of local knowledge and culture. We recommend combining this corpus with appropriately sourced natural Indic text and evaluating the resulting mixture for the intended use case.

Quality assessment is primarily automated, complemented by sampled human review whose coverage varies across languages. For the twelve-language workflow (Figure 2), the translator also serves as the judge. Retained text can still contain errors, and the ten-language workflow needs broader native-speaker validation. Source-ID checks remove processing duplicates; they are not semantic deduplication of similar content.

Alongside the corpus, AI4Bharat at IIT Madras, with support from NVIDIA, is building Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite, an open and evolving collection of benchmarks for Indic model capabilities. It helps model builders assess both task performance and language quality. See the companion blog, Better Models Need Better Benchmarks: Introducing Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite.

Explore the language configurations, test a training mixture, or adapt the open recipe to a new domain. Sharing per-language results and improvements to the generation workflow can help the community build on this work.

The companion reports, [*Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs*](Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs.pdf and the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Lightning technical report, provide the corpus accounting, generation methods, experiments, and evaluation details. Evaluation is the other half of this work. For the benchmark side, see the companion blog from AI4Bharat and NVIDIA, Better Models Need Better Benchmarks: Introducing Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite.

This work brings together NVIDIA, IIT Madras, AI4Bharat, and Bodhan AI. We also acknowledge the model and tooling contributions used in the pipeline: Google's Gemma, Bodhan AI's Indic Translate, and NeMo Data Designer. Additional NVIDIA data resources are available in the Nemotron Pre-Training Datasets collection.

作者： AI4Bharat — Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan、Mitesh Khapra、Anoop Kunchukuttan。NVIDIA — Niket Agarwal、Raviraj Joshi、Anusha Kamath、Markus Kliegl、Yev Meyer、Sriharsha Niverty、Kiran Praveen、Utkarsh Vaidya。

我们很高兴推出Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1 ，涵盖22种印度语言，约2.8万亿个代币，即将与用于创建它的开放式GPU加速数据生成管道一起发布。这些是印度宪法中列出的22种语言： 97 ％的印度人的第一语言，或2011年人口普查中的近12亿公民。此版本由英伟达与印度首屈一指的工程学院IIT Madras及其AI4Bharat实验室共同开发，为模型构建者提供了用于Indic预训练的大量新资源。管道捕获全代配方，包括提示、LLM工作流程和质量检查，因此开发人员可以根据自己的源材料进行调整，并生成更多数据以满足他们的需求。

IIT Madras的印度语言研究实验室AI4Bharat为印度语言构建开源数据集和模型。它的资源，如Sangraha ，是22种印度语言的开放式预训练语料库，为开放式印度语言模型研究奠定了基础。我们的联合开源版本代表了开放合成Indic培训数据的实质性扩展，该数据将提供给社区。它将精心策划的英语材料（包括数学、代码和问答内容）广泛混合到印度语言中，为团队提供了更多用于构建模型的培训材料，这些模型可以用这些语言解释技术概念、解决问题并回答问题。每个记录都可以追溯到策划的源文档，每个输出都会根据其输入进行检查，因此合成文本始终以真实信息为基础。
领导AI4Bharat并入选2025年TIME100 AI榜单的Mitesh Khapra指出了核心问题：印度语言技术落后于英语，因为“我们没有足够的印度语言数据。“我们正在用更多的数据来回应这通电话，以及一个开放的配方来产生更多的数据。
语料库还解释了人们的写作方式。它包括所有22种语言的本机脚本数据和12种罗马化文本，涵盖34种语言脚本配置。我们的工作流程将文档级翻译、质量评估和有针对性的维修与检查相结合，以保留方程式、表格和代码等内容。这些数据补充了自然撰写的印度语文本，这对于当地知识和文化背景仍然至关重要。
我们正在分享开放式生成配方，以便社区不仅可以复制数据，还可以进一步开展这项工作。团队可以直接使用语料库，调整提示和质量检查，或将自己的源文档带入工作流程。通过开放数据和流程，我们的目标是使大规模的Indic数据生成更容易访问，并使更多的开发人员能够为跨印度语言的更强大的模型做出贡献。
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL的继续预训练增加了100亿个Indic代币，这些代币来自该语料库的12种语言子集和自然的Indic文本。我们关于该型号的技术报告涵盖了整个故事。我们计划在未来的Nemotron模型中建立此语料库。
图1.语料库包含26010亿个原生脚本令牌和2246亿个罗马化令牌。计数使用Gemma-4标记器。文档记录包括共享来源的翻译和脚本变体；它们不是唯一的英文文档的计数。
语料库有两组语言配置：
在这里，母语脚本描述了书写系统：文本仍然是从英语翻译而来。罗马化是指用拉丁字母书写的印度语文本，而不是英文翻译。对于十二种双字母语言中的每一种，罗马化都涵盖了可接受的母语翻译的一个子集。
在构建训练混合物时，这种区别很重要。原生记录和罗马化记录提供不同的脚本曝光，但可以表达相同的基本内容。令牌计数描述保留的语料库，包括可接受的重写，而不是训练运行的令牌预算。计数还取决于所使用的标记器，因此语料库和训练令牌计数应单独读取。

为了构建此语料库，我们从15个Nemotron-CC-v2子集的文档开始，涵盖网络文本、问答材料、数学、代码和其他专业内容。我们使用NVIDIA的开源框架NeMo Data Designer来生成合成数据，以运行翻译、质量检查和有针对性的修复。在整个工作流程中，我们会保留每个源标识符，以便开发人员可以将输出追溯到其原始文档。像这样清晰的来源是使开放数据能够进行审计和构建的部分原因。图2显示了十二种语言的工作流程。
图2.十二种语言的四阶段Indic合成数据管道，使用NeMo Data Designer和Gemma-4-31B-it实现。我们翻译英语文档，评估翻译质量，修复低分输出，并将接受的翻译子集转换为拉丁文字。其他十种语言使用单独的Indic Translate工作流程，如下所述。
对于这十二种语言，我们完整地翻译文档，以便模型可以跨段落、表格和方程式使用上下文。我们通过比较完整文档上的模型、检查翻译质量和保存技术内容来选择Gemma-4-31B-it。我们的提示区分要从要保留的内容翻译的散文，包括代码、方程式、URL和格式。

翻译后，我们使用相同的模型根据其英语来源评估每个输出。多维质量指标（ Multidimensional Quality Metrics ， MQM ）是一个按类型和严重程度对翻译错误进行分类的开放式框架，其涵盖含义、流畅性、术语、风格和格式。我们仅保留得分至少为75分（满分100分）的输出（评分标准得分，而不是准确率百分比）。对于得分较低的输出，我们使用评估反馈来指导维修，然后根据相同的阈值重新评估它们。此过程在原生脚本和罗马化数据中恢复了4384亿个令牌，已包括在语料库总数中。抽样人工审核和测试，故意引入错误，有助于识别遗漏和残留的英语，为我们的提示和检查提供改进的信息。
可接受的母语翻译也为罗马化数据提供了起点。我们将子集转换为拉丁字母，并根据其原生字母输入检查每个结果。这将翻译与脚本转换分开。在我们最初的人类比较中，这种两步法比直接从英语生成罗马化文本产生更少的幻觉添加和更少的剩余英语。

对于其他十种语言，我们调整了工作流程，以解决在比较中观察到的长文档质量和脚本稳定性问题。我们使用Indic Translate进行翻译，这是由IIT Madras孵化的非营利性教育人工智能中心Bodhan AI提供的英语和22种印度语言的文档级翻译模型。Gemma-4-31B-然后根据其英语来源评估每个翻译。对于八种语言，我们采用全文档方法。对于较长的Santali文档，我们翻译重叠的窗口并重建文档；对于Manipuri ，我们翻译成孟加拉文字，然后转换为Meitei Mayek ，其原生字母。这些工作流保留至少75分（满分100分）的输出，并仅生成原生脚本数据，无需基于反馈的重写。
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL技术报告将Indic继续预训练（ CPT ）之前的检查点与该阶段之后的检查点进行了比较。配置的预算为1000亿个培训代币，其中10 ％ （ 100亿个代币）分配给合成和自然印度语文本的混合物。其余90%保持前述训练混合物的相对比例。
在所有五个报告的Indic知识和推理基准上得分都有所提高： MILU、Indic MMLU-Pro、Indic ARC-Challenge、Indic ARC-Easy和Indic GSM8K。
图3. Indic CPT阶段前后的Nemotron 3.5 Super VL。收益从4.98到9.82个百分点不等。比较报告了结合合成和自然Indic数据的训练阶段的变化，而不是孤立合成语料库的贡献。语言覆盖率因基准而异；这些是阶段级检查点，而不是最终模型版本的比较。
资料来源： Nemotron 3.5 Super VL技术报告，表2。GSM8K不包括Odia ，因为评估超过了服务上下文限制。
这些收益支持综合和自然印度语CPT配方，同时让其他模型和语言的混合选择进一步学习。
配套的Indic报告使用12种语言组的首次通过可接受数据来检查源混合物、合成数据池大小和脚本覆盖率。评估完整的语料库，包括恢复的重写和其他十种语言，仍然是那些对照研究的下一步。
除了CPT阶段的结果之外，发布的模型与上一代相比如何？图4比较了Nemotron 3.5 Super VL和Nemotron 3 Super在Indic任务性能和语言质量方面的比较。这些结果反映了发布的模型的完整培训流程，包括Indic CPT和培训后。
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL在所显示的六项任务基准中的五项上得分更高，涵盖知识、推理、数学、代码和翻译。遵循IFEval 1.5的说明下降了2.04分。它还改进了IndiVibe的所有四个维度：实用性、流畅性、语言和脚本保真度以及适当的详细程度。IndiVibe是Sarvam AI的印度语言助理式提示的开放基准。总之，这些评估检查了模型可以做什么以及它用印度语言进行沟通的程度。
图4.指示Nemotron Super各代的任务绩效和语言质量。左：六个任务基准。右：初步的IndiVibe条件偏好评分，而不是直接的直接赢率。标签显示百分比的变化，但使用chrF点的WMT24 + +除外。有关基准和评估详细信息，请参阅配套的Indic技术报告。
从模型所需的语言和脚本开始，检查样本，并在培训前查看数据集卡和许可证。配置使用语言、脚本和区域标签：例如， hi-Deva-IN在梵文中表示印地语，而hi-Latn-IN表示罗马化的印地语。
下面的示例从数据集卡中询问存储库ID ，然后发现可用的拆分并流式传输示例。
拥抱人脸数据集支持流媒体，因此读者无需下载整个语料库即可检查记录。发布可用后，固定数据集修订版以进行可重现的实验。
对于第一项培训研究，以固定的代币预算比较混合物，并记录自然/合成和本地/罗马化份额。跟踪每种语言的结果以及英语能力保留和语言/脚本质量。创建保留拆分时，请考虑来自不同语言和脚本的相同来源的记录。
要构建更全面的配方，请将语料库与Nemotron训练后数据配对，例如Chat & Instruction或Post-Training Blends集合。对于特定于印度的合成数据，种子NeMo Data Designer与Nemotron-Personas-India ，英语和印地语的合成人物角色，以印度的现实世界发行为基础。
适用于NeMo Data Designer的开源Nemotron Bharat翻译插件提供翻译和评估提示、可选的基于反馈的重写、文档窗口化和脚本重映射支持。使用其配置参考选择模型和语言，将提示调整到您的域，并设置重写参数。随附的开发人员备注解释了工作流程和工程选择。
从您自己的源文档的一小部分样本开始。检查翻译质量以及代码、数学和格式的保存，然后在扩展之前与母语审阅者一起完善提示和检查。将生成和语料库接受视为单独的步骤：插件返回候选人和分数，而过滤策略确定哪些记录进入训练语料库。
翻译可以扩大对原始材料的访问，但不能取代最初用印度语言编写的文本，也不能保证覆盖当地知识和文化。我们建议将此语料库与适当来源的自然印度语文本相结合，并针对预期用例评估所得到的混合物。
质量评估主要是自动化的，辅之以抽样的人工审核，其覆盖范围因语言而异。对于十二种语言的工作流程（图2 ） ，译者也担任评委。保留的文本仍然可能包含错误，十种语言的工作流程需要更广泛的母语者验证。源ID检查删除处理重复项；它们不是类似内容的语义重复数据删除。
除语料库外， IIT Madras的AI4Bharat在NVIDIA的支持下，正在构建Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite ，这是一个开放且不断发展的Indic模型功能基准集合。它有助于模型构建者评估任务性能和语言质量。请参阅配套博客Better Models Need Better Benchmarks: Introducing Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite。
探索语言配置，测试培训组合，或将开放配方调整到新领域。分享每种语言的结果和对生成工作流程的改进可以帮助社区在这项工作的基础上更进一步。

配套报告[* Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs *] （ Scaling Synthetic Pre-training Data and Evaluation for Indic LLMs.pdf和Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Lightning技术报告）提供了语料库核算、生成方法、实验和评估详细信息。评估是这项工作的另一半。有关基准方面，请参阅AI4Bharat和NVIDIA的配套博客，更好的模型需要更好的基准：介绍Indic-LLM-Eval-Suite。

OpenAI’s ChatGPT Atlas browser is gone, but now ChatGPT’s Google Chrome extension is getting some upgrades that allow it to use the browser tabs you already have open. With the extension installed, OpenAI says ChatGPT can now view your browser tabs when you tag Chrome in ChatGPT’s web or desktop app, posting a demo video showing someone asking ChatGPT to compare the three tabs they have open with sofas they’re considering.
Here are some of the sample queries OpenAI listed for using the upgraded add-on:

It’s also updated ChatGPT in the sidebar, with “the full power of ChatGPT” and your entire conversation history in Chat or Work to use without leaving the page you’re viewing. It also enables ChatGPT Work to “control” your Chrome tabs for tasks like “sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files,” similar to Google’s Gemini-powered “auto browse” feature, as well as organize or group open tabs.

All three of these technologies (along with the underlying base model) are composed into one model, taking up approximately the same amount of VRAM on a GPU as the base model would by itself. That means more capabilities with fewer GPUs.

And because the Switch adapters were built as cache-efficient Activated LoRAs, the KV cache created from a base model generation can be reused for any subsequent adapter-based decisions. Combined with our team's recent vLLM contributions to speed up low rank adapter inferencing, as well as a co-located ASR encoder, Granite Switch 4.1 models can switch between a chat request and a decision request and a spoken request, with blazing fast speeds.

Check out our Speech-to-Decisions HF space where granite-switch-4.1-8b transcribes audio, generates summaries, screens for harmful content, and tests 15 other user-defined flags—all running on a single endpoint in real time.

Decision models aren’t new. Our previous release of Granite Libraries features a repository of specialized “decision model” adapters and other specialized task adapters that can be composed into custom Granite Switch models. And while Jev and other closed decision models focus on generality, we’ve found that many of our specialized granitelib adapters can outperform generalists on specialized classification tasks.
Compare granitelib adapters with generalist decision models when evaluated on specialized classification tasks.

Because adapters share the base model's KV cache, adding specialists alongside a generalist decision adapter costs almost nothing. You get broad coverage from the generalist and higher accuracy from specialists on the tasks you care about.

In a “Race” between Granite-Switch-4.1-30B (frozen base Granite + 4 specialized aLoRAs) and Jev-27B (frozen base Qwen model + 1 generic decision LoRA), Granite-Switch-4.1-30B was able to complete a real world, 5-step RAG workflow much faster than its competitor.

Granite-Switch-4.1-8B and -30B are released with “batteries included”. They are Granite Switch models that we compiled with a predefined set of helpful adapters. But you don’t need to use our version. Anyone can compose their own Granite Switch model, mixing and matching adapters from Granite Libraries to best meet their needs.

Moving forward, we see tremendous opportunity for the community to compose and extend Granite Switch models with custom and third party adapters. We plan to release an Adapter SDK for training adapters in Mellea, along side other tutorials and Granite Switch support. These adapters could be specialized classification adapters to augment decision-based workflows or adapters for specialized language tasks. You could even use custom adapters to teach a 3B parameter version of Granite to play the classic game Doom.

Similarly to Jev, our custom 3B parameter Granite Switch model made split second decisions to navigate the Doom game, but was able to do so at 60 - 100 decisions / second, compared to Jev’s reported 10 decisions / second.1 Unlike Jev, this Granite Switch model can also narrate and respond to your questions while it is playing.

Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.

Alongside the launch of the company’s new AI wearables from Bee, Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk more in depth about where he sees personal computing headed.

“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”

By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.

“As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people … you’re not afraid if you miss something. It’s incredibly powerful,” Panay said.

Amazon’s biggest entry into this space is the set of new Bee devices it introduced on Thursday, which include a band you can wear on your wrist or detach to wear as a pendant, as well as a new credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of your smartphone.

These gadgets passively record audio and take notes about your day, finding the to-dos, reminders, and insights you may later need to refer back to. To balance the need to be useful with user privacy, Bee’s devices don’t actually store the raw audio from your conversations; they process the audio in real time and then delete it when done. Transcripts of conversations are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls. That means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you intentionally share them.
Panay said that privacy was a key consideration for how these new ambient devices should work.

“You have to give customers that control,” he said. “Every product is different, but for Bee specifically, as an example in the ambient space like that, you have to design with privacy in mind. And that’s what we do. That’s critical.”

The executive, who came to Amazon after 19 years at Microsoft where he oversaw the development of Surface devices, has spent a lot of his life thinking about how personal computing will evolve. With Bee — and ambient computing more generally — Panay also envisioned a future where the idea of interacting with apps becomes less important, as more tasks are handled via AI.

“Do I think we have a future where there’s a bit of a balance — a whole generation that doesn’t say ‘give me the app’ for that, but says it should just understand what I need? Yeah, I do. I think that transformation is coming. I think that is the next generation,” he said.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the smartphone itself won’t continue to be an important personal computing device (as much as Amazon would like it to be an Alexa tablet or Echo smart speaker), Panay pointed out. Rather, he believes a new crop of devices will emerge that use sensors to understand users better, and to bring intelligence to the world around you.

“I’m not a proponent that says one form factor is going to replace another. I don’t think that’s the case,” he clarified. “I think there’s an intelligence layer that connects it all … and it has to be useful.”

亚马逊将赌注押在环境计算上，而不是应用程序上，作为个人人工智能的未来。
除了 Bee 推出该公司新的人工智能可穿戴设备外，担任亚马逊设备、Alexa 和 Leo 高级副总裁的 Panos Panay 周四在 TechCrunch Disrupt 上登台，更深入地谈论了他对个人计算发展方向的看法。
“很多时候，你现在所做的事情——我们现在所做的事情——就是我们必须记住我们要求我们的工具为我们做什么，”帕奈开始说道，并解释说这就是我们与现代智能手机互动的方式。 “这就像瞄准，射击，返回，”帕奈继续说道。 “我认为我们正在走向一个以环境设备开始的世界。”
他所说的“环境设备”是指那些在后台安静工作的设备，使用传感器和人工智能来帮助你弄清楚需要做什么，而不是相反，你告诉设备你需要做什么。
“由于它在后台运行，你能够更加专注于当下。你能够完成更多工作。你将花更多时间与人相处......如果你错过了什么，你就不会害怕。它非常强大，”帕奈说。
亚马逊进军这一领域的最大举措是周四推出的一套新 Bee 设备，其中包括一条可以戴在手腕上或拆下作为吊坠佩戴的表带，以及一款信用卡大小的新设备，可以通过磁力吸附在智能手机背面。
这些小工具被动地录制音频并记录您的一天，查找您以后可能需要参考的待办事项、提醒和见解。为了平衡实用性和用户隐私的需求，Bee 的设备实际上并不存储对话中的原始音频；他们实时处理音频，然后在完成后将其删除。对话记录使用您的设备创建和控制的密钥进行加密。这意味着包括亚马逊员工在内的其他人都无法访问这些文件，除非您有意共享它们。
帕奈表示，隐私是这些新环境设备如何工作的一个关键考虑因素。
“你必须让客户有控制权，”他说。 “每种产品都是不同的，但对于 Bee 特别来说，作为这样的环境空间的例子，你在设计时必须考虑到隐私。这就是我们所做的。这很关键。”
这位高管在微软工作了 19 年，负责 Surface 设备的开发，后来来到亚马逊，他一生都在思考个人计算将如何发展。对于 Bee（以及更广泛的环境计算），Panay 还设想了一个未来，随着更多任务通过人工智能处理，与应用程序交互的想法变得不再那么重要。
“我认为我们的未来是否有一个平衡——整整一代人不会说‘给我应用程序’，而是说它应该只了解我需要什么？是的，我认为。我认为转变即将到来。我认为那是下一代，”他说。
Panay 指出，这并不一定意味着智能手机本身不会继续成为重要的个人计算设备（就像亚马逊希望它成为 Alexa 平板电脑或 Echo 智能扬声器一样）。相反，他相信将会出现一批新的设备，它们使用传感器来更好地了解用户，并为您周围的世界带来智能。
“我不支持说一种外形尺寸将取代另一种外形尺寸。我认为情况并非如此，”他澄清道。 “我认为有一个智能层可以连接这一切……而且它必须是有用的。”

cards.title: The next developer interface is ambient intelligence
cards.title_cn: 下一个开发者界面是环境智能
cards.summary: 【GitHub】For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools ch…
fulltext: For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools changed, but the relationship did not. Like most developers, I learned commands, memorized shortcuts, and adapted my thinking to the machine.

AI is changing that relationship and not because I can prompt my way to some workable code. It’s more because the system behind it can understand a repository, choose the right model, plan work, use tools, edit files, run commands, inspect failures, and keep going within boundaries the developer controls.

We’ve made it possible for a developer to describe an outcome, and GitHub Copilot can gather repository context, inspect symbols and dependencies, edit files, run tests, and revise the implementation. In the IDE, agent mode keeps that loop interactive. GitHub Copilot coding agent can take an issue into an isolated GitHub Actions-powered environment and return a pull request for review. This is not just faster coding. It is the shift from issuing commands to making intent executable. The developer still owns the outcome, but the work looks subtly different.

AI-assisted development compresses that chain of events. We spend less time navigating tools and more time setting direction, supplying context, defining constraints, and reviewing evidence. The development workflow now is about understanding the structure of codebases, the customer, and what a good solution should feel like.

This makes developers’ jobs even more important, and their time more valuable. It makes judgment more valuable. It makes taste more valuable. An agent can generate three implementations before you finish your tea, but someone still has to decide whether the abstraction belongs, the migration is safe, the tests prove anything useful, and the result solves the problem.
That is the most important change in the craft: the developer remains accountable for the outcome, even as more mechanics are delegated.
So what does this mean for the emerging developer workflow? The goal is to embed AI into the workflow, not beside it. It’s more of an ambient intelligence.

That requires portable context. MCP connects agents to tools and services; repository instructions and skills encode conventions; hooks enforce policy and validate output. Simpler interfaces need explicit context underneath.

I see three layers: modality captures intent; the harness plans and acts; the control plane lets developers inspect, redirect, and approve. The best products connect all three without surrendering control.
Together, they let developers move across text, voice, and physical controls without losing context.

I, and many others in the maker community, have been experimenting with ambient control devices, from inexpensive hackable picture frames to ESP32 devices with screens attached. Agentic coding is past just a keyboard and a terminal into alternative interfaces.

Getting this kind of technology into everyone’s hands is something that I’m very passionate about and so over the past 18 months we’ve been working with Logitech on their MX Keypad and how it can help this new way of working.

The Logitech MX Keypad turns familiar developer actions into programmable inputs to accelerate workflows that are ambient and contextual to the work devs are doing. In GitHub Copilot app, a key can submit a parameterized prompt, open or resume a Copilot session, invoke an IDE command, or trigger a multi-step sequence. The hardware earns its place only when that shortcut removes enough friction to keep you in the code, but still gives you control.

Physical controls work when an action repeats often enough that removing a few steps preserves concentration. Not every developer needs another device on the desk, and not every interruption deserves a key. However, with this experience the developer decides which actions earn that shortcut and when the keyboard, command palette, or voice is better. Maintaining flow is the key, and a good interface gives some of that attention back.
GUIs made software visual. Mouse made navigation easier. The web made it connected. Mobile made touch natural. Agents add intent and action. The interface now includes ambient control.

That is why GitHub worked with Logitech to integrate the GitHub Copilot app directly into the experience. Developers can run agentic workflows in control, map a repeated prompt, start or resume a session, and decide through real use whether a physical control helps you stay in flow.

This is still early, so the important questions are engineering questions. How much repository and organizational context should an agent retain? Which tool calls can run automatically? How should credentials, network access, and secrets be scoped? What evidence should accompany a change? How do multiple agents coordinate without duplicating work or creating conflicting pull requests? Products such as MX Keypad let us explore one practical part of that system: how developers invoke, steer, and resume agentic work without losing focus.

For decades, developers learned to speak computer: syntax, commands, APIs, shortcuts, and the occasional incantation copied from a seven-year-old issue comment. Now computers are getting better at meeting us halfway. The best interface will not have the most panels or AI buttons. It will understand enough context, preserve meaningful control, and get out of the way so we can build software that matters.

The goal is not to remove developers from the work. It is to remove friction around the work. Pairing MX Keypad with GitHub Copilot Pro+ gives developers a concrete experiment: choose one repeated interruption, map it to a control, and see whether it preserves focus.

fulltext_cn: 在我职业生涯的大部分时间里，构建软件都是从相同的设置开始的：键盘、鼠标、编辑器、终端、浏览器，以及我稍后肯定会看到的大量选项卡。工具改变了，但关系没有改变。像大多数开发人员一样，我学习了命令，记住了快捷方式，并使我的思维适应机器。
人工智能正在改变这种关系，并不是因为我可以提示我找到一些可行的代码。更重要的是，它背后的系统可以理解存储库、选择正确的模型、计划工作、使用工具、编辑文件、运行命令、检查故障，并在开发人员控制的范围内继续运行。

我们使开发人员能够描述结果，并且 GitHub Copilot 可以收集存储库上下文、检查符号和依赖项、编辑文件、运行测试以及修改实现。在 IDE 中，代理模式使该循环保持交互。 GitHub Copilot 编码代理可以将问题放入隔离的 GitHub Actions 支持的环境中，并返回拉取请求以供审核。这不仅仅是更快的编码。这是从发出命令到使意图可执行的转变。开发人员仍然拥有结果，但工作看起来略有不同。
人工智能辅助开发压缩了这一事件链。我们花更少的时间使用工具，而花更多的时间设定方向、提供背景、定义约束和审查证据。现在的开发工作流程是关于理解代码库的结构、客户以及好的解决方案应该是什么样的。
这使得开发人员的工作变得更加重要，他们的时间也变得更加宝贵。它使判断更有价值。它让品味变得更有价值。在你喝完茶之前，代理可以生成三个实现，但仍然需要有人来决定抽象是否属于、迁移是否安全、测试证明任何有用的东西以及结果是否解决问题。
这是工艺中最重要的变化：即使更多的机制被委托，开发人员仍然对结果负责。
那么这对于新兴的开发人员工作流程意味着什么呢？目标是将人工智能嵌入到工作流程中，而不是旁边。它更像是一种环境智能。

我看到三个层次：模态捕捉意图；安全计划和行动；控制平面允许开发人员检查、重定向和批准。最好的产品将这三者连接起来，而又不放弃控制权。

让每个人都能掌握这种技术是我非常热衷的事情，因此在过去 18 个月里，我们一直与罗技合作开发他们的 MX 键盘，以及它如何帮助这种新的工作方式。

当一个动作重复得足够频繁，以至于移除几个步骤可以保持注意力集中时，物理控制就会起作用。并非每个开发人员都需要在办公桌上放置另一台设备，也不是每次中断都需要一把钥匙。然而，凭借这种经验，开发人员可以决定哪些操作可以使用该快捷方式，以及何时键盘、命令面板或语音更好。保持流程是关键，良好的界面可以回馈部分注意力。
GUI 使软件变得可视化。鼠标使导航更容易。网络让一切变得互联。移动使触摸变得自然。代理添加意图和行动。该界面现在包括环境控制。
